Mbappe, Vini and Konate obscure Real's Ceuta message
- Published
Kylian Mbappe, Vinicius Junior and Ibrahima Konate rolled up their pre-game T-shirts ahead of Real Madrid's match at Elche on Tuesday to obscure the message of support for the people of Ceuta.
Ceuta is a Spanish autonomous city on the North African coast, bordering Morocco and separated from mainland Spain by the Strait of Gibraltar.
Players from both sides walked on to the pitch at Elche's ground, Martinez Valero, wearing white T-shirts carrying the message "Todos somos caballas" – translated as "We are all Ceutans" – along with references to the Spanish autonomous city.
While most of the players wore the shirts fully, Mbappe, Vinicius and Konate had theirs rolled up to around chest height, obscuring some of the slogan.
Mbappe and Vinicius then removed their shirts before the pre-match handshake, while Konate kept his on for longer. Their team-mates and the Elche players continued to wear the shirts through the pre-match formalities.
This is not the first time Real Madrid have shown support for Ceuta. Before their Champions League meeting with Inter Milan at the Santiago Bernabeu on 8 September, supporters in the south stand displayed cards featuring the coat of arms of the autonomous city, while the rest of the stadium joined the tribute with a round of applause.
The initiative was part of a wider show of support for Ceuta, following a major migration crisis in the Spanish territory after thousands of people entered from Morocco.
At least 72,000 migrants crossed from Morocco into Ceuta on 30 and 31 July. Most swam around a border fence and at least 100 people died during the crossing, according to figures from Ceuta's mayor.
Although most returned, as many as 5,000 remain in makeshift camps or are sleeping on the city's streets and beaches, leading to unrest in the autonomous Spanish city in North Africa.

Air pollution spiked after the Trump administration stopped embassy monitoring
Growing up in Shanghai in the early 1990s, Eric Zou remembers the air.
"I lived a couple of miles next to a chemical plant and it was just really bad, really foggy," he says. "It's the middle of the day, but you can't see the sun."
Intensive industrial activity blanketed many cities in China during the 1990s and 2000s with extremely hazardous air. But Zou, now an environmental economist at the University of Michigan, says that many people didn't really understand this smog as air pollution, or something that could harm them.
"When you have a big smog event, people often talk about that as fog, they think it was just like bad weather," says Zou. One big key to changing that sentiment, he says, was information initially provided by the United States.
In 2008, U.S. officials installed an air quality monitor on the embassy in Beijing and began making the information public. Over time, that helped spur demand for cleaner air, says Zou. "Once you have pollution information, it tends to be that it actually helps people to realize, 'Oh, I actually value air quality.' "
Since 2008, the State Department's monitoring initiative has expanded to more than 80 embassies and consulates. Research suggests that monitoring contributed to measurable improvements in air quality, especially across many low- and middle-income countries with limited monitoring systems of their own.
But in March 2025, the Trump administration shuttered that program, citing monetary costs. Research out this week suggests the move had health costs for the people living in those countries. Over the several months following the shutdown, air pollution levels measured via satellite increased by 24-33%, researchers reported Monday in the journal PNAS.
The State Department did not respond to a request for comment in time for publication.
"It's a great study, high quality. And it's a real pity," says Andrea La Nauze, an environmental economist at Deakin University in Australia who has researched the benefits of the program, but wasn't involved in this study. The program "led to sustained improvements in air quality that were continuing to increase after 10 years," she says.
She says this new research suggests those improvements aren't guaranteed if monitoring stops.
Measuring the consequences of not measuring
When Zoe Yiyuan Zhou first heard the news that the Trump administration was shuttering the embassy air quality monitoring, it struck her as a research opportunity.
"It's such a rare case to study this drawback," says the Columbia University climate researcher. While there's ample evidence of the benefits of increased monitoring, she says there aren't many examples of a sudden falloff of surveillance.
Zhou and her colleagues decided to compare air pollution levels before and after monitoring ceased across 46 cities. Since they didn't have on-the-ground measures of air quality for the latter part of that comparison, they used satellite data for both.
The team found no significant trends in air pollution over the 300 days preceding the end of U.S. reporting. But about three to four months after reporting ended, pollution had gone up, on average by about 30%. Satellite data isn't a perfect substitute for monitors that can measure on-the-ground pollution. The researchers estimate their satellite measurements translate to about a 4% increase in PM2.5 — the small suspended particles that can enter the lungs and bloodstream and cause health problems.
"That magnitude is certainly concerning," says La Nauze. "Particulate matter is a serious and dangerous thing, and being exposed to it is not good."
The increase was highest in Southeast Asian cities, including Manila, in the Philippines, Rangoon in Myanmar and Vientiane in Laos, says Zhao. Pollution also spiked more in cities with fewer monitoring alternatives.
The study can't say why pollution increased after monitoring stopped.
For countries with nonexistent or nascent monitoring programs, U.S. data may have prompted more regulatory action, says Zou. "Maybe the U.S. Embassy was a really strong force, in terms of a third-party auditing mechanism, and once that's removed, people are like 'Now I can just pollute, right?'"
In many industries, it costs money to cut down on pollution, says Zhou. When monitoring stops, companies may see it as an opportunity to cut those costs.
But the researchers did find some potentially hopeful news. Pollution levels seemed to go back down somewhat after peaking about three or four months after monitoring stopped.
It's difficult to say why this decrease happened, Zhou says, or whether the trend will continue. She suspects that it may reflect other forms of monitoring, by individuals or local governments, coming online in the wake of the U.S. withdrawal.
But not all areas may have the ability to readily make up for what's been lost, she says, especially in regions where air quality monitoring is new.
"Data is just so important," says Zhou. "Having access to information is necessary to make sure that these previous gains can continue. Public information creates accountability."

Ranking the greatest all-time fantasy football icons
- Published
Scanning the newspaper, inky fingers and fuzzled minds, scrambling for the calculator and jotting down the codes for Julian Dicks and Juninho. These lads will carry the team until you remember to pick up the house phone and cash in a transfer a few months down the line.
Before templates and triple captains there was a world of fantasy football that existed by writing out your XI and ringing in the names. Parents used it as a summer-holiday maths lesson.
Yet whether in print or online, there's nothing quite like the satisfaction of unearthing an absolute bargain. That free-kick taking defender, the undervalued forward, out-of-position goal-getter or cheap keeper posting clean sheets.
Since it began for the 2002-03 season, Fantasy Premier League has evolved into a huge database boasting millions of players across the globe, with substitutions and wildcards and the maths done for you.
But who, over the past quarter of a century of the competition's official game, are the biggest icons of all time?
With the help of our resident FPL expert Thomas Woods and some extensive research by the Fantasy Football Scout, that's what I'm digging into this week.
Based on stats and a touch of sentiment - Michu, we see you - I've ranked my top 10 below. We'd love to hear your thoughts in the comments, too.
Firstly, let's look at what makes a player iconic. Is it purely posting massive numbers? Thierry Henry's total from the inaugural season, for example, still ranks seventh overall. Indeed the Arsenal man was top scorer in three of the first four campaigns, but also the most expensive.
Frank Lampard, arriving late in the box, topped the charts three times with his goals from midfield for Chelsea, while the twinkle-toed Cristiano Ronaldo did it twice at Manchester United. The pair rank fourth and fifth for best individual seasons, respectively.
It's tempting to say we should discount such "obvious" picks for this debate, but then there's Mo Salah. The Liverpool asset might have eaten up a decent chunk of your budget, but packed guaranteed points for those premium pounds.
As the Fantasy Football Scout explains, since the game began, 52 players have reached 200 points in a season at least once. Salah has done it eight times. And the Egyptian is the only player to ever top 300 points. In fact, he's done it twice.
So Mo probably deserves a go. But we're really searching for those who have offered the most value over the years - cheap picks who seriously delivered.
Some went on to become Premier League stars, others became cult heroes, one-season wonders or bargain buys who got virtual tongues wagging.
10. Harry Kane, Tottenham, 2014-15, starting price £5m
England captain and record goalscorer, three-time Premier League Golden Boot winner. Harry Kane was hardly a secret at Tottenham, right?
After a series of loans and having not yet established himself at White Hart Lane, the young Spurs striker began the 2014-15 campaign as a likely £5m back-up to Emmanuel Adebayor and Roberto Soldado.
Kane didn't find the net until November in the Premier League, a 90th-minute winner after coming off the bench at Aston Villa, but it was the first of 21 goals in the competition that season as the homegrown striker established himself in Mauricio Pochettino's side.
As the Fantasy Football Scout notes, an eight-match run from gameweek 18 to 25 saw Kane notch 77 points with nine goals, four assists and 16 bonus points.
For those who gambled on him early, Kane proved a bargain. He rose from £5m to a peak £6.4m, racking up 191 points and ranking 11th on the all-time value list, despite playing fewer minutes than all those above him.
9. Charlie Adam, Blackpool, 2010-11, £5m.
The great budget enabler. Blackpool's Charlie Adam took penalties, free-kicks, corners and would probably have had goalkicks too if they let him.
He'd had a good season in the Championship, scoring 16 times, but no one really gave the Seasiders any hope on their Premier League debut and thus there was little expectation on the Scottish midfielder from FPL bosses.
Despite Ian Holloway's outfit eventually succumbing to the drop, Adam delivered a points tally that was only bettered by Manchester United's Nani that season - on the back of 12 goals, his 192 stood as the highest score by a promoted player at the time.
8. Michel Vorm, Swansea, 2011-12, £4m
Michel Vorm conceded four goals on his Premier League debut. That stacks up for a £4m keeper, you might think. Yet the Dutchman made 11 saves that day at Manchester City, more than anyone else would manage in a single game that season.
Vorm swept Swansea City's end-of-term awards but also became a FPL legend in the process. He made saves but also kept clean sheets, 14 of them in total, and earned the second-most points for a goalkeeper behind City's Joe Hart, who started the game £3m more expensive.
The Dutchman peaked in price at £5.3m and was the fourth-most owned player in the game at one point. Both virtually and in real life, it would be his standout season.
7. Stuart Dallas, Leeds, 2020-21, £4.5m
Under Marcelo Bielsa, Stuart Dallas was a FPL dream.
Racking up defensive clean sheets while operating further forward than his listed position suggested, cheap as you like, and even doing it against league heavyweights Manchester City, where he scored twice for 17 points.
"The Northern Ireland international's versatility played into the hands of FPL managers because, even though he was a classified as a defender, he played all over the place for Leeds in 2000-21 - more often than not as an attacking midfielder," explains Woods.
"And for a starting price of £4.5m you got eight goals, 12 clean sheets, three assists and a total of 171 points. Bargain."
6. Michail Antonio, West Ham, 2019-20, £7m
Michail Antonio is a curious pick, but deserves FPL cult hero status for one of the most memorable months in the game's history.
Classified as a midfielder but deployed up front, Antonio's value actually dropped during a campaign that was disrupted by injury and the coronavirus pandemic.
Following the restart, Antonio was unstoppable. He played seven times in July 2020, scoring eight goals. Incredibly, four of those came in West Ham's 4-0 away win at Norwich, where the midfielder posted a 26-point haul.
That's the joint-most on record for a player valued under £7m, alongside Cole Palmer, and only three off Salah's overall record for a single gameweek.
5. John Lundstram, Sheffield United, 2019-20, £4m
Lord Lundstram, as he was fondly known, didn't notch a season total as high as some on this list, but his bargain price, out-of-position listing and the fact he seemingly appeared from nowhere, having only made five starts for the Blades the previous season, saw him achieve legendary status in FPL.
"A £4m defender is usually the last spot on FPL managers' benches but Lundstram was misclassified by FPL towers and was actually a box-to-box midfielder," says Woods.
"He scored five goals and delivered four assists while picking up clean sheets along the way to 144 points, with his two-goal 21-point haul in week 11 particularly memorable.
"And being able to start a £4m asset allowed managers to cram more talent into the rest of the team too."
4. Riyad Mahrez, Leicester, 2015-16, £5.5m
Riyad Mahrez was a goldmine for Claudio Ranieri and FPL bosses alike during Leicester's title-winning season. As the Fantasy Football Scout notes, he flew out of the blocks with a 15-point haul in week one against Sunderland, rewarding the 5.9% of managers who started the season with the winger in their side.
It was no fluke. Mahrez made double figures in five of the opening six gameweeks, his 56 points among the best starts ever to a FPL campaign. Inevitably, other managers jumped on board, and by week seven Mahrez was in more than 50% of teams.
Jamie Vardy, of course, had a dazzling season of his own, returning a goal or an assist for 15 weeks on the bounce, though he started £0.5m more expensive than his team-mate.
Mahrez finished the campaign as the top scorer in FPL with 240 points, despite his modest starting price.
3. Michu, Swansea, 2012-13, £6.5m
Of course, there is a certain amount of nostalgia and sentiment to FPL. We gaze proudly at these little icons clocking up points like they're family.
Michu was the epitome of an on-screen cult hero, going from relative unknown to bagging 190 points, his price rising by £2m throughout the year.
As Woods says, he is probably the biggest one-season wonder in FPL history.
"A few savvy managers picked up on the fact the Spaniard had scored 15 goals in La Liga the season before and had him on the opening day when he scored twice at QPR," adds our resident FPL expert.
"He was effectively a £6.5m striker classified as a midfielder. It felt like he was in most managers' teams by the time he ended 2012-13 with a whopping 18 goals.
"He managed two the following season... and then left for Napoli."
2. Mohamed Salah, Liverpool, 2024-25, £12.5m
OK, firstly, other Liverpool assets were perhaps unfortunate to miss out on this list - flying full-backs Trent Alexander-Arnold and Andy Robertson were consistently must-have picks.
Luis Suarez, meanwhile, boasts the third-highest score ever and, as the Fantasy Football Scout points out, he notched a record 55 attacking returns in 2013-14 despite missing the first five games.
But if we can allow one premium pick, it has to be Salah. And if we have to pick a season, it must be his record-breaking 2024-25 campaign when the Egyptian produced a staggering 344 points.
Remarkably, it came off the back of his lowest score the year before - although low for Mo was still upwards of 200 points. Salah, simply, is FPL royalty.
1. Cole Palmer, Chelsea, 2023-24, £5m
You have to put Cole Palmer's 2023-24 season into context. He wasn't a household name, like now, having left Manchester City for more gametime at Chelsea.
The youngster began the season as a £5m midfielder and did not start a game for the Blues until matchweek seven. In fact, as the Fantasy Football Scout explains, only 63,575 managers owned him (0.6%) for his first double-figure return at Burnley the following week.
That crept up to 4.5% for his next 12-pointer at Tottenham in gameweek 12, which then triggered a surge in popularity as FPL bosses lumped on Stamford Bridge's new star.
More than five million owned Palmer when he scored four goals against Everton during a 26-point haul in gameweek 33, albeit he still only cost £6.1m.
"Based on starting price, Cole Palmer in 2023-24 is the best-ever value player in Fantasy," concludes the Scout.
Palmer finished as the season's top scorer with 244 points and was handed the biggest price rise in FPL history of £5.5m, meaning he cost £10.5m at the start of the 2024-25 campaign.

The performance gap between frontier AI models from US tech companies and the best open-weights models from Chinese companies has closed to just 4.4 months, according to a Mozilla report. That explains why many companies are shifting to the significantly cheaper open models for routine work—and helps reveal a narrow band of workloads where frontier models are worth the cost.
Most organizations should ideally be using open models as the default for the majority of their work, according to the latest State of Open Source AI report from Mozilla, published on September 15 and shared with Ars prior to publication. The report highlights how a leading open model, Moonshot AI’s Kimi K3, achieves a composite AI performance score on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index that is just three points behind Anthropic’s Fable 5 closed frontier model, all while costing just 30 percent of the latter.
“Closed earns its premium in a few places: expert professional work, high-intensity retrieval, and long context,” Raffi Krikorian, chief technology officer at Mozilla, said in an email to Ars. “We see the decision to pay for closed as workload-specific rather than organization-specific.”
The open-weights AI models allow anyone to download the main model components and run the models on their own computers, but developers still typically withhold vital information such as training data, the data pipeline, and training code. By comparison, US tech companies such as Anthropic and OpenAI mostly offer closed frontier models that keep everything proprietary, requiring customers to pay more for access.
Organizations still pay for closed frontier models because they work out of the box and come bundled with “compliance packaging, support, and accountability,” whereas many organizations lack the staff to run open-weights models well, Krikorian explained.
But the steadily narrowing performance gap between open and closed frontier models, coupled with the cost-effectiveness of open models, is now widely recognized by many companies. For example, the delivery company DoorDash has been using Kimi for routine work while reserving Fable for more difficult tasks that would normally take human experts longer to complete.
The narrowing performance gap is being measured in several ways. For example, the research nonprofit METR has defined an AI model’s time horizon as the length of tasks—measured by how long human experts require to complete them—that can be handled by AI models with a “reliable” 50 percent success rate. That time horizon has been doubling on a set cadence that has accelerated over time.
The best closed model can currently do a job that is 1.7 times as long as the longest job that the best open model can reliably finish.
“If the open frontier can handle a seven-hour job, the closed frontier can handle a 12-hour one,” Krikorian told Ars. “In four months, the open model handles the 12-hour job, and the closed one handles something around 20.”
Tasks requiring between eight and 12 hours are typically the ones that a closed frontier model can do and the open models cannot handle yet, Krikorian said. No models are generally capable of reliably doing tasks longer than 12 hours, whereas tasks taking less than eight hours can be done by either type of model and could be handed off to the cheaper open models.
There are many nuances and caveats for such comparisons. For example, closed frontier models often come with their own harness—the software layer that helps the models access various tools and memory to perform agent-like actions. Harnesses custom-built by AI labs for their models can sometimes boost performance on various tasks, whereas the models may perform less well with third-party harnesses.
To level the playing field, the benchmarking company Vals AI has been evaluating different open and closed models by using its own neutral harness. When every model ran on the same harness in the Terminal-Bench 2.1 evaluation, the open-weights model GLM 5.2 from the Chinese company Z.ai (Zhipu AI) scored within a point of Anthropic’s Claude Opus 4.7 and 4.8 while costing about five times less per completed task.
In other words, paying for closed frontier models buys about a four-month head start at about five times the per-task cost—but only when currently looking at tasks taking between eight and 12 hours.
“Pay when that head start is worth it, something like a deadline that lands before the open frontier catches up would be here,” Krikorian told Ars. “Routine work you’ll still be doing next quarter is not, because you’ll be able to do it for a fifth of the cost soon, and the model won’t be the bottleneck anyway.”
Concentrations of power
The surging popularity of open-weights models can be seen on OpenRouter, the AI gateway and marketplace that gives developers access to hundreds of different models from multiple providers. The Mozilla report noted that eight of the top 10 models ranked by token volumes in August 2026 provide open weights.
However, open models are still lagging behind closed frontier models in revenue. A paper by Frank Nagle and Daniel Yue for the Linux Foundation found that open models earned just 4 percent of overall revenue compared to closed models getting 96 percent of revenue—although they were looking at data from May through September of 2025.
“In the last year, open models have exploded, so we do expect revenue to have shifted,” Krikorian said.
The current reality is that “most of the open models the world runs on are Chinese,” Krikorian said. “The Chinese labs are running the same playbook the Americans ran with Android—give it away, but own the ecosystem around it,” he explained.
But Krikorian is not so concerned about “Chinese models” as he is about the risk of concentration. At the moment, the best open models are concentrated in China, whereas the best closed frontier models come from US companies. He argued for US and European labs to start competing in the “same open lane, so that no single country sets the world’s defaults.”
“The uncomfortable truth is that the plural ecosystem around open-weight AI is largely funded by Chinese capital right now,” Krikorian said. “That’s a plurality and a concentration at the same time.”
The history of development for open source software such as Linux may offer some lessons for how an “alternative coalition” could come together, Krikorian said. Such open source software infrastructure was funded by a coalition of organizations that “each needed the commodity layer to exist,” including neutral foundations.
Any coalition for building more open AI models would likely consist of “institutions with a mission rather than a market,” as opposed to frontier AI labs, Krikorian said. He described it as follows:
We need public compute programs funding fully open reference models. Switzerland’s national compute producing Apertus is an example. Foundations need to hold the same neutral ground that they held for the internet’s open protocols, extended into models, harnesses, and agentic standards. Companies that benefit from commodity models have to participate. And philanthropy has to cover what none of the others will—evaluation and audit infrastructure, especially.
Krikorian also called for the alternative coalition to go even further than open-weights models by embracing more of the open source approach. “It’s hard to fully trust a model with decisions if you can’t tell how it was trained or what it was evaluated against,” he said.

When I teach the structure of cancer to first-year medical students, I go well beyond the causes and mechanisms of the disease. Medicine has changed since my own siloed training in pathology. Now many medical schools leap into humanism. In addition to learning about pathophysiology, cancer genetics, bloodwork, scans, and symptoms, students where I work meet a cancer patient, the patient’s family, and oncologist. They come to understand the decisions, treatments, and emotions that followed a difficult diagnosis and prognosis.
The patient they learn about is me. The tumors, test results, and treatments I present? Mine.
I don’t want to lose a single opportunity to make medicine very, very real for the next generation of physicians. They deserve medical training where there is a real person behind every scientific concept, and so do their future patients. Every biopsy result or slide is just a slice (sometimes literally) of a person just like me.
In 2017, I was diagnosed with thymic cancer. Thymic cancer is both rare and aggressive, accounting for less than 1% of all cancer diagnoses and about 0.2% to 1.5% of all malignancies. I’m currently in treatment after a recurrence. I’ve been an intriguing, nine-year case study, almost from the moment of diagnosis.
“Almost,” because I was diagnosed with a mass on a Thursday, had a biopsy on Friday, and received my diagnosis from a pathology lab on Saturday. Stunned silence filled those three days. I simply … stopped talking. I withdrew.
On Monday, my wife and a friend took me to see the oncologist, who asked questions that I wouldn’t or couldn’t answer. They filled in the blanks for me as I sat, not communicating.
Exasperated with my silence, my oncologist abruptly said, “David, come with me.” She took me from the office, alone, and brought me into an examining room. She asked me a few more questions that I didn’t answer.
“I have cancer,” she said. “So don’t think for one second that that I don’t know how you’re feeling right now.”
My catatonic state fell away, and I was able to communicate again within minutes. Something like hope crept toward me when my oncologist was vulnerable about her own health. She was not obligated to be so open, but her humility unlocked me. It allowed purpose to come into focus.
From that moment, it became a no-brainer to present my own journey to medical students. But now I’d also found a co-teacher who watched me go from despondent and nonresponsive, to accepting what became a nine-year (so far) quest for understanding and healing.
I, too, was not required to share my own case, but I felt doing so in class might offer future doctors a deeper level of understanding. I saw no reason for physicians-in-training to wait till residency to understand how anxious patients can become when a test is ordered or additional bloodwork is drawn, or to hear what it’s like to wait with family for results or insurance clearance.
That’s why, once I’ve discussed the foundational concepts of cancer, I show students my biopsy slide, the stain used to determine the origin of the cancer I have, and my X-rays, CT scan, and MRI and PET scans. I let silence set in as the class digests the information, before I take questions that range from the diagnostic to the emotional. Two weeks later, my oncologist joins us to discuss our feelings and approach.
Students’ response to this approach has been full of gratitude, curiosity, respect, and a yearning for growth professionally and personally. They’re beginning to understand the medical concepts they need to memorize as well as the very personal impact they’ll have on their own patients someday.
Sharing my health challenges has been one of the most fulfilling and full-circle choices I’ve made: Students who have learned from me rotate through my oncologist’s practice, and several are my current physicians.
Sidestepping an opportunity like that would have been walking past a door God had opened. Even if I don’t understand my circumstances every day, and I don’t, I accept that I’m in God’s hands. I have faith in today’s doctors-in-training, too, and feel a unique responsibility to them and the generations of patients they’ll treat throughout their careers.
What I want for today’s medical students is what I hope we all seek in our doctors: to become learned and wise, to grow into compassionate educators who ensure patients understand every medical challenge as they face it and choice before they make it. One unchanged fact about the field of medicine is that practitioners need to embrace lifelong learning, whether it’s a robotic surgical technique, artificial intelligence, a new virus, or knowing when to sit with a grief-stricken patient. In those moments, we physicians draw on all our capacity to be present, and to employ fundamentally human and uniquely godly compassion.
I’ve been fortunate to create a blueprint from what God has handed me, remembering as I undergo treatment that I can keep working with excellence and empathy to hopefully shape medical students’ perspectives. I hope they come to understand the value in showing up for patients and colleagues, even when life feels out of control and explanations for circumstances seem inadequate. If my experience helps future physicians care for generations of patients with deep knowledge and compassion, I’ll take it as a victory for both humanity and holiness.
David Elkowitz, D.O., is a professor of pathology and laboratory medicine and science education at the Donald and Barbara Zucker School of Medicine at Hofstra/Northwell. He also serves as the school’s associate dean for academic programs and educational culture and as director of the Academy of Medical Educators.

3 people killed when NBC news helicopter crashes while covering Los Angeles bus accident
TV anchor confirms that the station's helicopter went down during live broadcast
A local NBC news helicopter crashed in a Los Angeles neighbourhood on Tuesday and burst into flames, killing at least three people while reporters were covering the nearby crash of an SUV and a city bus, officials and the station said.
Colleen Williams, an NBC4 Los Angeles anchor, confirmed during live broadcasts that the station's chopper went down just before 7 p.m. and two people on the helicopter were killed.
"We are going to take a couple of minutes to think about that, process it," she said, her voice shaking with emotion. Moments later their coverage abruptly cut off.
Fire officials, Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass and other politicians spoke during a news conference Tuesday night but gave no details on who perished in the crash. After the news conference, the mayor and other officials embraced a crying NBC reporter who also was hugged by fellow journalists.

"Losing five Angelenos is very painful," Bass said. "And I know this community of Chatsworth hit hard, will be grieving for some time."
The helicopter crashed near a large storage facility in the neighbourhood of Chatsworth in the San Fernando Valley, as news crews were covering the bus crash that left at least two people dead and six others injured, according the Los Angeles Fire Department.
At least one person killed in the helicopter crash was outside in the parking lot next to the commercial building, said Capt. Branden Silverman, a spokesperson for the Los Angeles Fire Department.
Helicopter 'destroyed'
Two people were transported to a hospital, said Rico A. Gross, a fire department battalion chief. Their conditions were not immediately released.
"From the helicopter itself, it's pretty well destroyed," Silverman said. "So we are going to have to go through the rubble and see how many victims there were on board, as well as identify the helicopter; we couldn't even see a tail."
At least four cars and two storage containers on the ground burned after the helicopter caught fire, which was quickly put out, according to officials.
About two hours before the crash, an SUV slammed into the middle of a city bus, killing at least two people and injuring six others. Photos and videos online showed half the SUV lodged into the side of an MTA bus.
NBC has confirmed the helicopter was NewsChopper4, which is operated by Angel City Air, and was used by NBCLA and Telemundo 52. The outlet said several TV news helicopters were reporting on the bush crash before the news chopper went down about 2.4 kilometres from the bus collision.
NBC4 and Telemundo 52 Los Angeles said in a statement they "are deeply saddened" to learn of the helicopter crash and extended "heartfelt condolences to the families, friends and colleagues of those who lost their lives."
Gov. Gavin Newsom thanked the emergency crews responding to both crashes and said in a post on X that "our hearts are with the victims and families."
The National Transportation Safety Board and the Federal Aviation Administration said it will be investigating the cause of the helicopter crash and would be sending one of its investigators on Wednesday.
There have been at least eight fatal crashes involving news helicopters in the U.S. since 2000, killing 16 people, according to a review of federal accident records and news accounts.

The world is bracing for a “super” El Niño, and its effects are already being felt in India, where the monsoon has brought less rain than average but more intense downpours.
Meteorologists predict that the current El Niño, which is developing over the Pacific, could be one of the strongest in living memory. India is likely to be heavily affected, particularly later in the monsoon, when El Niño’s influence tends to strengthen.
But, as Ligin Joseph of the University of Southampton explains in The Conversation, its effects on India’s monsoon are not straightforward. A previous study in Science found that El Niño tends to bring more extreme summer monsoon rainfall to India.
This year, the southern state of Kerala has felt the brunt of the building super El Niño, with about a fifth less rain than normal. Yet intense downpours in the first week of August triggered flash flooding and landslides, killing 26 people.
The super El Niño is expected to peak after India’s monsoon season, but Indians are already keeping an anxious eye on the skies, wondering where and when the next deluge may come.

Canon's R8 II camera borrowed its styling from a classic SLR film camera
t's now Canon's lightest full-frame camera with 5-axis stabilization and can shoot at 40 fps.
Though preoccupied with vlogging lately, Canon hasn't forgotten its photography market. The company just unveiled the 24-megapixel EOS R8 II, an entry-level full-frame camera with all new styling that's strikingly different from the previous R8 model. In fact, the new camera reaches back much further, borrowing design cues from its classic EOS 650 SLR film camera, adding a touch of retro chic to a previously dull design.
A few things you may notice about it are the much more squared-off design compared to the rounded, swoopy R8. With the optional battery grip installed, it has an angled right corner like the 650 and more horizontal shutter button area. That said, it's significantly larger and more modern-looking than its muse. As for controls, it has a joystick to move the autofocus point that the R8 sadly lacks.
Canon told Engadget that it addressed issues that myself and other reviewers found wanting in the R8. First off, it's faster. The R8 II can now shoot at 40 fps in electronic shutter mode with continuous autofocus and auto-exposure, and capture more shots in a burst (58 percent more JPEG and 30 percent more RAW images). And unlike the previous model, it's equipped with 5-axis in-body stabilization that reduces shake up to 7.5 stops with supported lenses. It's also the lightest full-frame camera on the market with this feature at 1.2 pounds (546 grams).
The autofocus has been overhauled as well. Equipped with Canon's Dual Pixel CMOS AF II, it offers 100 percent coverage and subject tracking of people, animals and vehicles, while delivering more tenacious tracking than the EOS R8, Canon said. It also comes with a feature we've only seen on higher-end models like the EOS R6 III: the ability to register specific people for tracking. You also get pre-continuous shooting that allows the capture of up to 20 frames (a half second's worth) before fully pressing the shutter button.
Video hasn't changed much, but was already pretty powerful with the R8. You can capture 4K 60p video that's oversampled from the full 6K sensor width, as before, along with uncropped 1080p video at 180 fps. It supports 10-bit 4:2:2 capture with Canon Log3 in HEVC or AVC codecs at bit rates up to 250 Mbps. Video autofocus is much improved, with all the same tracking and subject detection AF features as for photos.
Other features include new Positive Filmtone, Negative Filmtone and Night Scene film looks, an A+ Automatic Exposure feature with a blurred background setting for movies, a separate Slow & Fast mode, a single UHS II card slot and enhanced stabilization modes for video. The 3-inch 1.62-million-dot vari-angle rear display and 2.36-million-dot EVF are basic, as is the LP-E17 battery that allows for just 340 shots in power saving mode.
The Canon EOS R8 II is now on pre-order for $1,899, with shipping set to start in late October. You may find that price a bit shocking for an "entry level" model, but it appears to be the new normal for cameras in a world of inflation and tariffs. You can also get it in a kit with Canon's RF24-50mm F/4.5-6.3 IS STM lens for $2,099. The optional EG-E2 Extension Grip is $100, and Canon's new Speedlite EL-5 Ver.2 flash will set you back $379.

Police fire tear gas to break up Congo protests against constitutional changes
Police in Congo have broken up opposition protests using tear gas against hundreds of demonstrators
KINSHASA, Congo -- Police in Congo fired tear gas Tuesday to disperse hundreds of people demonstrating against constitutional changes they said could allow President Felix Tshisekedi to seek a third term in office.
The opposition coalition C64 organized demonstrations in the capital, Kinshasa, and several other cities, including Lubumbashi and Kindu in eastern Congo, despite restrictions on mass gatherings imposed due to the fast-spreading Ebola outbreak.
The protest in Kinshasa drew hundreds of people and began peacefully, but was dispersed by police with tear gas and warning shots after protesters clashed with pro-government supporters.
“The Congolese state is working with a political party militia,” said opposition leader Martin Fayulu. “God is great; I made it out alive. There was a massacre, and the police were firing at us.”
Congolese government spokesperson Patrick Muyaya condemned the opposition for disrupting activities by falsely claiming schools would be closed on Tuesday. “The right to protest is recognized in the Constitution, but it must be exercised properly,” he said.
Police also dispersed a June rally in Kinshasa that C64 organized against the constitutional changes. Several people, including Fayulu, were injured.
Congo is plagued by multiple crises, including an Ebola outbreak and an escalation of the decades-long conflict with the Rwanda-backed M23 rebels, one of more than 100 armed groups vying for control in the eastern provinces.
Tshisekedi, 62, has been in office since 2019 and is due to complete his second five-year term in 2028. He has said he would be willing to seek a third term if approved by voters in a referendum.
The Congolese Constitution bars any revision of presidential term limits. However, a bill under consideration in the National Assembly, a lower chamber, would allow the president to amend those provisions in the event of a “major dysfunction” that paralyzes state institutions, potentially following a referendum.
The country’s main opposition parties, which have been divided in recent years, joined forces in May under the banner of C64, or Coalition Article 64, to oppose what they describe as an attempt by Tshisekedi to remain in power. The coalition has called the proposed changes a “serious threat” to the country’s stability.

Opener Aneurin Donald will make his England debut in the first T20I against Sri Lanka at the Aegeas Bowl in Southampaton on Tuesday.

AI-native semiconductor verification startup VerifAIX has raised $5 Mn (about ₹48 Cr) in a seed funding round co-led by Endiya Partners and Bluehill VC. The round marks VerifAIX’s first institutional fundraise. The startup plans to deploy the fresh capital to accelerate product development, expand customer deployments, and grow its engineering teams across the US, India, and Israel. It will also use the capital to advance its proprietary “Formal Brain”, scale its automated abstraction and decomposition capabilities to larger chip designs, and strengthen its formal verification and simulation tools. Founded in 2024 by Madhulima Tewari, Kenneth Roe, and Avner Landver, VerifAIX is developing an AI-native platform to help semiconductor engineering teams verify chip designs. The fundraise comes as AI is increasingly being deployed across the semiconductor design workflow, including to generate register-transfer level (RTL) code and other design and verification assets. However, faster generation of hardware designs has also increased the need for systems that can independently establish whether these outputs conform to their original specifications. This is the gap VerifAIX is looking to address with what it calls a “verification trust layer” for AI-driven chip design. Inside VerifAIX’s Platform At the centre of its platform is the Formal Brain, which creates a mathematically grounded representation of a chip design and its intended behaviour. It analyses specifications, RTL code, and verification assets to identify inconsistencies and gaps. Unlike tools primarily focused on using large language models to generate verification code, VerifAIX said its platform combines AI-based reasoning with deterministic and mathematically rigorous verification. Its AI agents cover multiple stages of the verification process, including specification analysis, verification planning, testbench generation, formal analysis, simulation, coverage, and debugging. The platform also flags gaps and potential errors in specifications and recommends fixes. “AI is changing how semiconductor designs are created, but generating a design is not the same as proving that it is correct,” Tewari, CEO of VerifAIX, said. She added that the startup plans to build an independent verification layer that can establish the correctness of AI-generated designs while maintaining traceability to the original design intent. The startup is targeting semiconductor and chip IP companies, processor and AI accelerator developers, hyperscalers, and other custom-silicon developers. It views EDA vendors as partners rather than customers. India’s Growing Chip Ecosystem The development comes amid growing investor and policy interest in India’s semiconductor ecosystem, particularly across chip design, testing, and specialised components. Earlier this year, semiconductor startup HrdWyr raised $13 Mn to accelerate the development of its AI-native system-on-chip products and expand its global customer engagements. Meanwhile, the ecosystem has also begun producing exits. Last month, German semiconductor major Infineon agreed to acquire Peak XV-backed C2i Semiconductors for an undisclosed amount. The two-year-old startup builds power-management solutions for AI data centres and cloud infrastructure. The acquisition came months after C2i closed its Series A funding round at $16.7 Mn (₹160.5 Cr), led by Peak XV Partners, with participation from TDK Ventures and existing investor Yali Capital. On the policy front, the Union Cabinet recently cleared the second phase of the India Semiconductor Mission, Semicon 2.0, with an outlay of ₹1.28 Lakh Cr to strengthen the country’s chip design and manufacturing ecosystem. At the heart of this push is India’s semiconductor market, which is projected to grow from about $62 Bn in 2026 to $155 Bn by 2031, driven by domestic demand, policy support, and global supply-chain diversification.

Since the beginning of the Iran war in late February 2026, people have shared a video allegedly showing U.S. President Donald Trump in 1987 advocating to "go in" and take the Middle Eastern country's oil.
In the purported clip, Trump says of Iran, "You take their oil. That's what I'd do," adding, "You go in." Journalist Barbara Walters asks how he would take the oil, inquiring, "Would you take a chance in a war?" Trump responds, appearing to say a war would be inevitable even if the U.S. did nothing, telling her: "You're going to have a war. … You're going to have a war by being weak."
Users shared (archived) the video (archived) on Bluesky (archived), Facebook (archived) and X (archived), among other platforms.
In sum, the decades-old clip is authentic, meaning that it was not created with artificial intelligence or other digital fakery. Trump truly advocated for going into Iran in 1987, saying, "You take the oil. That's what I'd do."
Trump posted the video on Truth Social on March 30, as some users accurately pointed out (archived). The video in his post begins with him saying, "because I'm running for the presidency." A longer video shows he fully says, "I'm not here today because I'm running for the presidency."
The clip originates from an episode of ABC's "20/20" featuring a profile of Trump by Walters. Newspaper archives pin (archived) the segment's apparent air date as Dec. 11, 1987.
Snopes emailed the White House to ask whether the Trump administration wished to respond to users sharing the video and will update this article if we receive further details.
Days after reposting the clip, on April 3, Trump posted a message matching his stance from nearly 39 years before, saying he wanted to take Iran's oil:
With a little more time, we can easily OPEN THE HORMUZ STRAIT, TAKE THE OIL, & MAKE A FORTUNE. IT WOULD BE A "GUSHER" FOR THE WORLD??? President DONALD J. TRUMP
(Donald Trump via Truth Social)
Transcript of Trump's 1987 remarks on Iran
A lengthier video from the "20/20" segment appears on Vimeo and YouTube, with the part about Iran beginning just after the two-minute mark.
The longer clip features more details, including journalist Charles Bremner remarking on Trump's stance:
WALTERS (
voice-over ): But does Donald Trump want to be president? TRUMP (speaking to the Portsmouth, New Hampshire, Rotary Club): I'm not here today because I'm running for the presidency. I'm here because I'm personally tired of seeing this great country of ours being ripped off.
WALTERS (voice-over): But as far as Trump is concerned, our allies are only part of the problem. The real culprit is Iran.
TRUMP (speaking to the Rotary Club): Why couldn't we go in and take over some of their oil, which is along the sea?
WALTERS (speaking to Trump): How would you do that? Would you send in the Marines? Would you take a chance in a war?
TRUMP: Let 'em have Iran. You take their oil. That's what I'd do.
WALTERS: But how?
TRUMP: How?
WALTERS: I mean, do we want a war? What do you mean, we take their oil?
TRUMP: You go in… you go in…
WALTERS: How do we go in?
TRUMP: You're going to have a war. Barbara… You're going to have a war by being weak.
WALTERS: OK. How do we go in? What do we do?
TRUMP: Excuse me.
WALTERS: Yeah.
TRUMP: You're going to have a war, and it's going to start in the Middle East.
WALTERS: What if the Soviet Union said, "You do this to Iran, we're going to come in?"
TRUMP: I don't believe they'd do it. The next time Iran attacks this country, go in and grab one of their big oil installations, and I mean, grab it and keep it, and get back your losses, because this country has lost plenty because of Iran.
BREMNER (speaking to off-camera interviewer): Donald Trump seems to have a Clint Eastwood approach to foreign policy.
WALTERS (voice-over): Charles Bremner is the New York correspondent for the London Times. He wrote this article that appeared in the Times the week following Trump's New Hampshire speech.
BREMNER: He recommended strikes at Iranian oil fields. This obviously would create a great chain reaction across the area if it ever took place. And obviously, European allies would be appalled by any such behavior.
We messaged Bremner on X to ask whether he wished to share any new comment about the parallels of the video from the past lining up with the war and will update this article if we receive a response.
The report also notes that Trump took out a full-page advertisement in The New York Times (archived) and other newspapers in September 1987 with the title "There's nothing wrong with America's Foreign Defense Policy that a little backbone can't cure." The ad displays an open letter from Trump "on why America should stop paying to defend countries that can afford to defend themselves." It does not mention Iran.
For further reading regarding Trump in the 1980s, we previously reported about whether a photo shows Trump in Moscow, when he was 41, at the invitation of Yuri Dubinin, the Soviet ambassador to the U.S. We've also covered a number of instances in which Trump has posted inauthentic images and videos, often generated with AI, on social media.

iOS 27 focuses on useful refinements, with better Liquid Glass controls, smarter Siri AI, natural-language Shortcuts, Safari web-change alerts, separate alarm volume, improved Photos tools, AirPods EQ, smarter password handling, and several everyday quality-of-life upgrades.
Apple has finally started rolling out iOS 27 to all eligible devices after testing it in beta for months. If you are reading this article, the update is already rolling out. If your iPhone supports it, you can go to Settings, General, Software Update, and update to the latest version.
iOS 27 isn’t a significant jump from what we have seen from iOS 18 to iOS 26. For those who are not aware, Apple has changed the version names to match the year. So instead of iOS 19, they moved it to iOS 26 to match the year 2026.
This year’s iOS 27 is more about refinement and fixing the issues that came along with iOS 26.
One of the biggest updates for most people, at least based on our insight, is the ability to refine the liquid glass design. Apple is now offering a separate setting to make your liquid glass look more frosted or transparent, and also allowing you to set different volumes for the alarms.
Plus, there is a new Siri and plenty of other Siri AI features, such as creating your own shortcuts using natural prompts. Let your password app fix compromised passwords, monitor website changes for free using Safari, and much more.
I have been testing iOS 27 for a few months now, testing its wide variety of features. In this guide, you will learn about the 27 best iOS 27 features that everybody should know and use for a better quality of life.
Table of Contents
Best iOS 27 Features You Should Know and Use
There are tens of new feature additions and improvements in iOS 27. However, not every new feature deserves your attention. There are a few features that really stood out for me and are genuinely useful in day-to-day life that everyone should be aware of. So here are my ten favorite picks before going to the comprehensive list of features.
Adjust Liquid Glass Design Transparency
It is evident that most people hated the new liquid glass design Apple introduced in iOS 26. Apple made the entire UI transparent overnight with a glossy effect, which made text hard to read and was resource-heavy.
Additionally, a few apps failed to adapt to this design perfectly, resulting in a bad user experience. However, Apple didn’t back off from the decision. Since the launch, Apple has continued to refine the liquid glass design to make it better and more usable.
In the latest iOS 27 update, Apple is offering a separate setting that lets you adjust the transparency of the liquid glass design. This setting is different from what we have covered in our TechPP videos, and here is how to use it.
Build Your Own Shortcuts Using Natural Prompts
Extensions and shortcuts are the two easiest ways to add missing features, whether it’s on your iPhone or in any browser. However, creating shortcuts isn’t always an easy task. It involves dealing with plenty of elements and actions, which can be hard for a casual user.
But that’s changing with iOS 27. The new Siri AI will now let you create a new shortcut based on simple, natural prompts. Now you can simply describe a shortcut using natural language, highlighting what it can do. For instance: A shortcut that automatically changes your iPhone wallpaper every morning or a shortcut that reminds you to drink water every two hours.
Since it uses AI behind the scenes, the possibilities are endless. You can describe whatever problem or feature you want to add through the shortcuts, and it will do it for you. However, the current implementation is not reliable for complex extensions. But it is a good start, and it will only get better in future versions.
I found using Claude or Codex to create iPhone shortcuts is the most reliable way, and it works much better for me than using Siri to create shortcuts, which often don’t get the desired results I wanted.
Let Your Password Apps Handle Your Compromised Passwords
When Apple first introduced the Passcodes app in iOS 18, it was super basic and missed a lot of the features found on other passcode management apps at the time. However, Apple continues to add new features, and the recent iOS 27 brings the ability to fix your compromised passwords automatically.
In simple words, if any of your passwords are compromised, your password app will automatically renew them into new passwords without you having to do it manually.
Password management apps are very good at finding your compromised passwords in data breaches. However, previously you had to manually visit every site and change the password yourself. But that’s going to change with iOS 27, where you can simply tap to auto-change the password, and it does it for you.
Monitor Any Web Changes in Real Time
This is my favorite addition to the Safari browser. Probably a feature that can kill many third-party apps. Apple has added a new Notify Me feature to the Safari web browser in iOS 27. It lets Siri AI monitor real-time changes on the website and notify you. Whether it’s an e-commerce price drop, real-time stock changes, or even a new article addition to any webpage, Safari can monitor it for you.
The best part is, you can describe what changes you want to get notified about in a natural prompt, and it does it for you. Also, there are no hard limits on how many trackers or websites you can track, and it lets you track changes every hour. Weekly, monthly, or even daily. The only requirement is that your device should support the Apple Intelligence feature.
Set Separate Volume for Your Alarms
Another feature that Apple should have introduced years ago is the ability to set custom volumes for your alarms in iOS 27. Previously, Apple used to have a single volume for all sounds, including alarms, calls, media, and notifications. In iOS 27, Apple is splitting that up, letting you set separate volume levels for alarms, media, and notifications.
One-Tap Access for Your Wi-Fi and Mobile Data Toggles
If you are someone who frequently adjusts the mobile and Wi-Fi toggles on your iPhone, iOS 27 is getting a very big, useful upgrade. Now, without needing to open the toggle or the entire panel, you can just individually turn your Wi-Fi toggle on and off directly from the toggle. It is enabled by default.
If you have customized it, you can just drag and drop the new network panel to get access to these features.
Auto-Paste Suggestions on Top of Your Keyboard
Another feature that Android users have enjoyed for years is now finally available on iPhone starting with iOS 27. Once you copy text or take a screenshot, the iOS keyboard now automatically suggests the recently copied clipboard text and images, which you can simply tap on and paste wherever you want.
Previously, it required you to long-press, select, and tap on the paste option to do that.
New Custom Equalizer for Your AirPods
Apple is rolling out a custom equalizer in the settings for AirPods. Now, iPhones with iOS 27 have a native AirPods equalizer in Settings to help you customize the audio output.
The new custom equalizer allows you to adjust lows, mids, and high frequencies separately. However, it is only available for devices running on H2 or later Pro devices, and for older devices, users need to rely on Apple’s Adaptive EQ.
Quickly View Photos Captured by You
One of the biggest downsides of iOS Photos is that the images captured from your iPhone are mixed with screenshots, memes, and other downloaded images saved from third-party apps. This makes it extremely hard for you to find the photos captured particularly from your iPhone. In iOS 27, Apple has added a new “Captured by Me” folder to the Photos app. It only shows the photos and videos taken with your iPhone camera, letting you easily find them.
Let Your Earbuds Automatically Pause When They Detect You Have Fallen Asleep
If you use AirPods, Apple has added another useful feature in iOS 27: your AirPods can automatically pause music, podcasts, or whatever you are listening to when they detect that you have fallen asleep.
Most apps these days offer sleep timers that automatically pause after a certain time. However, Apple’s implementation is more dynamic and doesn’t rely on a set time limit. Based on your movement, the AirPods automatically detect when you have fallen asleep and pause the music. This can be extra useful if you are someone like me who falls asleep, and it also eliminates the need for you to set a sleep timer every night.
The Phone App Automatically Shows Relevant Information While You Are on the Call
How many times have you searched for specific information during a call with a service agent? If your answer is often, then Apple has added a very useful feature for you.
With iOS 27, the Phone app on your iPhone now automatically shows relevant information when you are on a call in real time. These include your reservation numbers, order details, confirmation codes, and much more, which Apple can fetch from other Apple services. This eliminates the need for you to search through emails, messages, or other apps while speaking to customer support or during a business call.
Apple’s Mail App Is Now Better at Finding Information
If you use Apple Mail, it is getting a useful update. Starting with iOS 27, Apple says Mail search is upgraded to find more relevant information based on your search.
Now, instead of remembering the exact subject lines, names, or even words in your email, you can just use your natural tone and search for the exact information you want. Apple says the Mail app can now display more relevant information at the top of the search results, and it’s also smarter, as it can automatically identify the query and find the relevant information.
Now, You Can Set an Exact Expiry Time for Your Find My Sharing
If you use Apple’s Find My for location sharing, it is getting a useful update. You can select the exact time when your location sharing should stop. Previously, Apple only allowed you to share your location for an hour, until the end of the day, or until you manually turn it off.
But with iOS 27, Apple is giving you more flexibility, letting you choose a custom time. Now you can set a combination of days along with the hours to share your location. This also eliminates the need for you to manually remember to turn off location sharing if you have set it to indefinitely.
Now, You Can Turn Your Physical Cards Into Digital Passes
Apple Wallet app in iOS 27 lets you convert your physical cards into digital cards and store them in your Apple Wallet. Carrying a physical card can be a hassle, especially if you have multiple cards. It not only makes your wallet bulky, but also makes it hard to find the right one when you need it.
Moreover, there is a high chance that you can forget it, and it could get lost. Now, with the ability to convert your physical cards into digital ones, the Apple Wallet app eliminates all of these pain points. Plus, even if you want to carry a physical card, I would highly suggest converting it into a digital one, which can come in handy sometimes.
Improved AI Writing Tools Across the System
AI writing tools were the first Apple Intelligence features Apple introduced in iOS 18. However, Apple left them out and forgot to update them in iOS 26.
But in iOS 27, with the overall improvements in the AI features and getting close to what it has promised, Apple has also upgraded AI writing tools throughout the system.
Now, these writing tools are more advanced and improved. The best part of these AI writing tools is that they are integrated directly into the workflow.
So if you want to summarize, shorten, or fix spelling mistakes, you don’t need to switch apps. You can generate, rewrite, or correct text directly from your iPhone keyboard. Plus, Apple is also integrating these AI capabilities across the system, including Mail and the Notes app, letting you easily access them anywhere.
Easily Create Calendar Events Without Specific Details
Creating a calendar event requires you to fill in separate details for title, date, time, location, and other details. However, with iOS 27, Apple is making it easy for you to create or edit calendar events.
Now, without needing to fill everything manually, you can just create a calendar event using natural prompts.
For instance, you can ask Calendar to create a birthday event at 4 a.m. tomorrow, and it will do it for you. Calendar app can now understand details such as important keywords, dates (such as tomorrow at 4 PM), a person’s name, and other key details, and automatically create a calendar event. Plus, you can also edit using natural language.
Connect an iPhone Directly to Gym Equipment
If you own an iPhone and want to track your workout data, pairing it with an Apple Watch is the most sensible decision. However, it is expensive and can be overkill for users looking for basic fitness tracking features who don’t need distraction on their wrist.
However, the Apple Watch has this nifty feature where they connect to your gym equipment and receives live workout data, such as your speed, distance, pace, resistance, and the duration of your workout, which you can then measure and analyze in your Apple Health app.
If you do not own an Apple Watch or don’t want to carry it during your workout, Apple in iOS 27 has added the same GymKit functionality directly on your iPhone. So now your iPhone can directly connect to your compatible gym equipment and receive the live workout data. Plus, if you have an Acura Pro 3, you can also connect and track your real-time heart rate information.
Pause Location Sharing Without Disabling It Permanently
If you use Find My to share your location with others, iOS 27 is adding the ability to temporarily hide your location without permanently ending location sharing completely.
In previous versions, if you wanted to temporarily stop sharing your location, whether it’s because your iPhone battery is running out, or if you are planning a surprise, or if you don’t want to reveal your destination, you needed to permanently stop location sharing.
With iOS 27, you can temporarily hide your location from a person. The best part is that the person does not need to be removed, and you also do not need to remember to turn the location back on after the situation has ended.
New Improved Cleanup Tool for Your Photos
I personally hate AI photo editing features inside the Photos app. Recently, both Apple and Google have added several features that are designed to alter and convert your photos into AI-generated ones. However, one feature that I found very useful is the ability to remove unwanted people or objects from a photo directly in the Photos app without relying on third-party tools.
However, Apple’s initial version of the Clean Up Tool isn’t as great as expected. It struggled to remove unwanted distractions from an image. However, with iOS 27, Apple has significantly improved it. Now it’s on par with other clean-up tools that perfectly edit the image naturally, without leaving smudges or empty patches.
Automatically Organize Safari Tabs by Subject
With iOS 27, Apple’s Safari browser can now automatically organize tabs for you. Many other browsers have adopted this feature, but it took some time for Apple to implement it.
If you use the Safari browser and have many tabs open, you can enable the Auto-Organize feature so that it automatically organizes your tabs. This lets you easily find them or close all of them at once.
Generate Your Own Extensions for Safari
Similar to iOS Shortcuts, you can also generate your own extensions using natural prompts in Safari. If you have an Apple Intelligence-supported iPhone, you can just visit the extension tab and give it a natural prompt about what exact features the extension might have, and Apple Intelligence will create a fully working extension for you.
You can just use this extension for an individual web page, or for all the web pages in your Safari browser.
New Siri for Agentic Tasks
Apple is finally close to delivering the Siri it promised two years ago. With iOS 27, Apple is introducing the new Siri, called Siri AI, which is now better at answering your questions and also better at agentic tasks. Plus, it can now search across your Apple apps, including Mail, Messages, Photos, Notes, and all other supported apps, and get information for you.
You can create a reminder, edit a message, organize details, or complete another task. Plus, Siri can also have better context, which means it can remember the information that it gets from other apps. Although at its current stage it is not as advanced as Gemini or other intelligent or agentic AI tools, it is a good start for Apple to deliver what it promised.
It will only get better from now on. Plus, Siri is directly integrated into the system. You can activate it from any screen. Plus, it is free to use without any limitations, except for a few features that Apple might put behind a subscription paywall in the future.
New Wallpaper Extensions
If you customize your iPhone and set a new wallpaper often, this can come in handy. Apple is introducing a new wallpaper extension feature in iOS 27, which expands your wallpaper so it fits correctly based on your iPhone dimensions.
In most cases, if your iPhone wallpaper doesn’t match your iPhone screen dimensions, it can look blurry and pixelated. Plus, if you want to set it as a lock screen wallpaper, it can also affect the depth effect, making the overall wallpaper look blurry and clumsy.
With this new extension wallpaper, Apple now extends the wallpaper to perfectly fit your iPhone’s aspect ratio. The best part is it preserves the main subject and only generates the matching scenery at the image’s edges, so that the subject stays in the middle without being cut off.
Reply Inline to the Messages From Android Users
With the iOS 27 update, Apple is putting an end to another discussion of blue and green bubbles and Apple’s tactics to limit RCS messaging.
Apple iMessage now supports inline replies, where you can directly reply to a specific message sent from your Android friend. This is like a nested reply where you can long-press on any message and tap on Reply. Along with your reply, the other person’s message appears on top, making it easy for them to spot and understand.
New Siri Visual Intelligence
Siri is also now upgraded with better visual intelligence, and it is now live inside your camera app. Now you can spot objects inside your camera and ask Siri to describe them. This can be especially useful for visual intelligence tasks, such as translating the text from a photo, identifying a specific object or food, or extracting the details from a flyer.
Plus, the best part is that, since it is being done by Siri, you can also ask follow-up questions and even delegate tasks, such as adding the extracted information to your calendar or splitting and storing it in any app. Now, adjust your lock screen clock to make it look smaller.
This can be small, but useful for people who often customize their lock screen.
Apple is now letting you adjust the clock size on your iPhone lock screen. Now you can adjust the size of the lock screen clock even smaller. If you feel your clock is covering the important details of your wallpaper, or if you want it to take up less space, you can simply use the smaller clock feature to adjust its size and make it look smaller.
Organize Your Photos Better
While Apple’s Photos app search is smart enough to find the relevant image you are looking for using just natural prompts, Apple is also letting you add individual star ratings and keywords to the photos. Starting with iOS 27, you can rate the photos up to 5 stars and add keywords.
Photos app displays these details while you are browsing your media library, letting these photos stand out from the rest. This makes them easy to spot instead of manually comparing photos to find the best ones from your extensive media library.
Save Photos Directly From Videos
With iOS 27, Apple also introduced the ability to save any frame from a video. You can simply use the Save frame as a photo feature, and the video frame will be saved as a photo. You can save multiple frames as photos.
Here is how:
- Open the Photos app on your Phone
- Play any video and tap on the three-dot menu at the top
- From here, tap on the Save Video frame as a photo option
Get the Most Out of iOS 27
